post.text: Shadman Rahman One extension that comes to mind, Right now: guardrails define boundaries, evals define quality.But the missing layer might befeedback loops from real usage. For example:-capturing how outputs actually get used-whether suggested actions lead to outcomes-feeding that back into evals over timeCurious, How do you define good enough in evals? Do these evolve per use case or stay standardized?

_debug.note: Source: Jahin Showic comment on Shadman's Crucible announcement post. Asks two questions: how do you define 'good enough' in evals, and do they evolve per use case or stay standardized.
